                        DIRECT TESTIMONY OF NIKOLAOS POLITIS
                           (Opposing Any Route Utilizing Link M22)

 Q:      Please state your name.

 A:      Nikolaos Politis.

 Q:      Where do you reside:

 A:      My current residential and mailing address is 2502 Dunlavy Street, Houston, Texas 77006.
         However, my wife and I spend a lot of our time at our retirement home in McCulloch County
         which is on Link M22.
 Q:      Are you an intervenor in this PUC docket?

 A:      Yes. My original intervention request was filed in this docket on April 6, 2026 under PUC
         Interchange Item No. 234. I filed a supplement to my intervention request on April 10 under
         Interchange Item No. 365. The ALJ granted my intervention request on April 17 in SOAH
         Order No. 5 (Interchange Item No. 757).
 Q:      Did you file a protective order certification entitling you to receive copies of Protected
         Materials including Highly Sensitive Protected Materials this docket?




Nikolaos Politis Exhibit No. 1-- Direct Testimony of Nikolaos Politis                        Page 1
  A:      Yes. Me and my attorney filed protective order certifications on April 17 under Interchange
         Item No. 658.
 Q:      What was the basis of your intervention request?

 A:      The fact that I would be personally affected by the location of the transmission line on my
         retirement home property in McCulloch County as Link M22 directly crosses my 167-acre
         property. In the Application Map Inset 3-1F-3 my property is labeled as Tract No. 831 and my
         retirement home is labeled as Habitable Structure No. 620.
 Q:      Please briefly describe your Tract 831 property and how you use it.

 A:      I have owned the property for the past eight years. I acquired it for use as a weekend and
         vacation home and also to use as my retirement home. It is a beautiful rural piece of property
         with four ponds, a water well, and abundant wildlife and vegetation native to the area. Now my
         wife and I travel to the property almost every weekend and we spend about 50% of our time at
         the property. Our two sons and our grandchild also frequently visit us there along with other
         guests. I also rent out a portion of my property to a neighbor for cattle grazing. I have made
         various improvements to the property such as sharing in the costs of a fence with my neighbor
         to the east.
 Q:      Please summarize your position in this docket.

 A:      I oppose the PUC’s selection of Route Nos. 295, 296, 297, 547 and 548 and any other route
         containing Link M22. I support Route No. 894 which is the route that best meets the applicable
         routing factors as described in the testimony of the Applicants’ routing expert Casey D. Petty.
         In my testimony I sometimes refer to Route 894 as the “Preferred Route”.
 Q:      Why do you oppose any route using Link M22?

 A:      First and foremost, because that link crosses on the north side of my property only about 160
         feet from my house and our water well. At that short distance, the transmission line on Link
         M22 would present substantial risks to the health of me and my family and our guests from
         radiofrequency (RF) emissions and extremely low frequency (ELF) magnetic fields associated
         with high voltage transmission lines. I understand that these health risks are intended to be
         addressed in the PUC’s policy of “prudent avoidance”, but it simply is not at all prudent to




Nikolaos Politis Exhibit No. 1-- Direct Testimony of Nikolaos Politis                         Page 2
          locate a high-powered transmission line so close to a residential home, especially when there
         are alternative more acceptable routes.
 Q:      What other concerns do you have about use of Link M22?

 A:      At the short distance of only 160 feet from my home, a 765-kv transmission line would be an
         aesthetic eyesore and would greatly devalue my home and property both now and in the future.
         It would also prevent me from making full use of the portions of my property subject to any
         transmission line easement that would be required. Moreover, the construction and
         maintenance of a transmission line on Link M22 would also severely disrupt my family’s quiet
         enjoyment of our property.
 Q:      Does Link M22 follow along the property line between your property and your neighbor’s
         property to the north labeled as Tract 833?
 A:      No, it does not. Link M22 diverges from my northern property line as it is situated about 150
         feet to the south of my northern property line and thus bisects my property instead of following
         the property line. I understand that this violates one of the PUC’s goals in transmission line
         routing. There is also an existing roadway easement following my northern property line, so it
         makes more sense for Link M22 to have been situated along the property boundary and the
         existing roadway, although regardless of any minor route adjustments that might be considered,
         I remain adamantly opposed to any route using Link M22.
 Q:      How does Link M22 affect land west of your property?

 A:      Link M22 appears to traverse multiple private tracts just to the west of my property rather than
         following established corridors such as U.S. Highway 190 where existing utility easements and
         transportation infrastructure already exist. Following established corridors minimizes land
         fragmentation and environmental disturbance. However, as I just stated, I am not advocating
         for any modifications to Link M22 as I remain opposed to any use of Link M22.
 Q:      Are there any other nearby habitable structures on Link M22?

 A:      Yes, there is another habitable structure on Link M22 located approximately 2,000 feet east of
         my property which is located only about 120 feet north of the proposed transmission line route
         on Link M22.
 Q:      Can you provide photos of your property and its relation to Link M22?



Nikolaos Politis Exhibit No. 1-- Direct Testimony of Nikolaos Politis                          Page 3
  A:      Attached to my testimony are three photos of my property that I took to try and demonstrate its
         existing beautiful rural atmosphere and the view toward Link M22 to the north of my home.
         The first photo is of my retirement home on Tract No. 831. The second photo is a view from
         my home looking directly north toward Link M22 which would be only about 160 feet away
         from my home. The third photo is a view from my home looking northeast past my water well
         toward the eastward section of Link M22.
 Q:      Why do you support the selection of the Preferred Route 894?

 A:      Because, as explained in the testimony of the Applicants’ expert witness Casey D. Petty, Route
         894 on balance best meets all applicable PUC routing criteria. For example, Routes 295, 296,
         297, 547 and 548 (which are all the proposed routes containing Link M22 and which I refer to
         as the “Link M22 routes”) all are more costly than the Preferred Route 894 as shown in
         Application Attachment No. 4 (cost estimates of all proposed routes). The least costly of the
         Link M22 routes is Route 295 which at $2,078,362,000 is still $1,975,000 more costly than
         Route 894 which is $2,076,387,000.
 Q:      Besides project cost, are there any environmental routing factors that favor the Preferred
         Route 894 over the Link M22 routes?
 A:      Yes. The number of habitable structures within 500 feet of the route centerline for the
         Preferred Route 894 is only 85 whereas the Link M22 routes all have from 104 to 153 habitable
         structures within 500 feet. Moreover, the Preferred Route 894 has the lowest of the following
         routing criteria as compared to all of the Link M22 routes:
             •    the lowest length of the route across potential wetlands;
             •    the lowest number of stream crossings;
             •    the lowest length of routes across lakes and ponds;
             •    the lowest number of recorded cultural resources within 1,000 feet of centerline; and
             •    the lowest length of right-of-way within the foreground visual of U.S. and state
                  highways.
 Q:      Are there are any other environmental factors that weigh against selecting a Link M22
         route?
 A:      According to the April 27 comments submitted by the Lone Star Chapter of the Sierra Club
         (Interchange Item No. 3365), the most northern routes roughly following U.S. Highway 190


Nikolaos Politis Exhibit No. 1-- Direct Testimony of Nikolaos Politis                          Page 4
          (east of Brady and to the north of Route 894) are better in terms of avoiding wildlife habitat
         fragmentation, river crossings, endangered species habitat and rough terrain, and also in terms
         of more closely following already disturbed land and existing highway routes. Assuming these
         comments are well founded, the Link M22 routes to the south of Route 894 are clearly not as
         good as the Preferred Route 894 and the other northern routes.
 Q:      Does this conclude your testimony?

 A:      Yes, but I reserve my right to respond to any other information that comes available and to
         rebut any testimony filed by any of the other Parties.




Nikolaos Politis Exhibit No. 1-- Direct Testimony of Nikolaos Politis                          Page 5
